---
title: "Iteratively reweighted least squares"
execute:
  warning: false
  message: false
---

Logistic regression has no ordinary least-squares solution because the inverse logit makes the likelihood nonlinear in the coefficients. **Iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS)** solves a sequence of local weighted least-squares problems. We can follow that sequence for the SuperTelicity verb-type model.

```{r}
#| label: irls-data
#| echo: true
st <- read.csv("data/supertelicity/supertelicity-cloze.csv")
st$verb_type <- factor(st$verb_type, levels = c("manner", "result"))
y <- st$prep_in
X <- model.matrix(~ verb_type, st)
glm_fit <- glm(prep_in ~ verb_type, family = binomial(), data = st)
```

At iteration $t$, let

$$
\boldsymbol\eta^{(t)}=\mathbf X\boldsymbol\beta^{(t)},\quad
\boldsymbol\mu^{(t)}=\operatorname{logit}^{-1}(\boldsymbol\eta^{(t)}),
$$

$$
w_i^{(t)}=\mu_i^{(t)}[1-\mu_i^{(t)}],\quad
z_i^{(t)}=\eta_i^{(t)}+\frac{y_i-\mu_i^{(t)}}{w_i^{(t)}}.
$$

The update is

$$
\boldsymbol\beta^{(t+1)}=(\mathbf X^\mathsf T\mathbf W^{(t)}\mathbf X)^{-1}
\mathbf X^\mathsf T\mathbf W^{(t)}\mathbf z^{(t)}.
$$

```{r}
#| label: run-irls
#| echo: true
beta <- rep(0, ncol(X))
path <- data.frame()
for (iteration in seq_len(5L)) {
  eta <- drop(X %*% beta)
  mu <- plogis(eta)
  w <- pmax(mu * (1 - mu), .Machine$double.eps)
  z <- eta + (y - mu) / w
  beta <- solve(crossprod(X, X * w), crossprod(X, w * z))
  path <- rbind(path, data.frame(
    iteration = iteration, intercept = beta[[1L]], result = beta[[2L]],
    log_likelihood = sum(dbinom(y, 1L, plogis(drop(X %*% beta)), log = TRUE))
  ))
}
path
stopifnot(max(abs(beta - coef(glm_fit))) < 1e-7)
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-irls-path
#| echo: true
library(ggplot2)
long <- rbind(
  data.frame(iteration = path$iteration, coefficient = "intercept",
             estimate = path$intercept),
  data.frame(iteration = path$iteration, coefficient = "result",
             estimate = path$result)
)
ggplot(long, aes(iteration, estimate, linetype = coefficient, shape = coefficient)) +
  geom_line(color = "#1F5A85") + geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(x = "IRLS iteration", y = "Coefficient", linetype = NULL, shape = NULL) +
  theme_classic()
```

The plotted path records successive local weighted-least-squares solutions. The working response $\mathbf z$ is algorithmic, whereas the observed response remains the original vector of *in* and *for* choices; the final coefficients agree with `glm()` to the asserted tolerance. Thus IRLS is local least squares, not a claim that the Bernoulli data have become Gaussian.
